The core of the CLI

The CLI's own commands: prepare a cluster, see how it is doing, and apply Reefs, Nereids, Mandates and profiles

O core do CLI

Os comandos do próprio CLI: preparar um cluster, ver como ele está, e aplicar Reefs, Nereids, Mandates e profiles

Opening · groups · 1/2

Eight groups, before any Reef

  • init: prepares the cluster, core and a profile
  • status: one row per Reef and its Nereid
  • doctor: one pass or fail per check
  • Reef: a capability, its kinds and its command group
  • nereid: the controller that looks after a Reef
  • mandate: binds a Reef to a Nereid, with its params
Abertura · grupos · 1/2

Oito grupos, antes de qualquer Reef

  • init: prepara o cluster, o core e um profile
  • status: uma linha por Reef e a sua Nereid
  • doctor: um pass ou fail por verificação
  • Reef: uma capacidade, os seus kinds e o seu grupo de comandos
  • nereid: o controller que cuida de um Reef
  • mandate: liga um Reef a uma Nereid, com os seus params
Opening · groups · 2/2

Eight groups, before any Reef

  • profile: the Reefs, Nereids and Mandates that come together
  • config: the SLO, the installation and your current owner
Abertura · grupos · 2/2

Oito grupos, antes de qualquer Reef

  • profile: os Reefs, Nereids e Mandates que vêm juntos
  • config: o SLO, a instalação e o seu owner atual
Init

How does a cluster become a Nereus instance?

Como um cluster vira uma instância do Nereus?

Init · init --generate-filebuilt

The settings of init, written once to a file

As configurações do init, escritas uma vez num arquivo

~/example
# Write the settings, and create nothing$ nereus init \    --create-cluster \    --name nereus-local \    --generate-fileSETTING            VALUE         SOURCEtarget             k3d           defaultcreate_cluster     true          flagname               nereus-local  flagingress_port       8080          defaultinstallation_name  nereus-local  cluster nameprofile            core          default✓ settings written to ~/.config/nereus/init.yaml: edit it, then run 'nereus init'

Reef · reef createbuilt

create fails on a Reef that exists, and says what changes it

Reef · reef createpronto

O create falha num Reef que existe, e diz o que o muda

~/example
# As kubectl create does$ nereus reef create release✗ reef release already exists. To change it, run one of:  nereus reef apply release                     # the version this CLI pins  nereus reef apply release --image <ref>       # an OCI package  nereus reef apply release --from-file <file or folder>

# What would change$ nereus nereid apply reference-release \    --image localhost:5111/reference-release-controller:0.1.1 \    --dry-runWould configure core/nereids/reference-release for reef release: image sha256:ffb8e8957c6e → sha256:3f2a9c1d7e4b.Nothing changed (--dry-run). # The new image$ nereus nereid apply reference-release \    --image localhost:5111/reference-release-controller:0.1.1✓ core/nereids/reference-release configured, Ready, pinned to sha256:3f2a9c1d7e4b (was sha256:ffb8e8957c6e): see 'nereus release --help'
Nereid · nereid apply --publishbuilt #1951

Only the endpoints a person grants are ever published

Nereid · nereid apply --publishpronto #1951

Só os endpoints que uma pessoa concede são publicados

~/example
# Let the edge Reef publish Triton's mcp endpoint$ nereus nereid apply triton \    --publish mcp✓ core/nereids/triton unchanged, Ready✓ core/nereids/triton configured (publishes: mcp) # Take the grant away$ nereus nereid apply triton \    --publish ""✓ core/nereids/triton unchanged, Ready✓ core/nereids/triton configured (publishes nothing)

Mandate

Which Nereid answers, and with which settings?

Mandate

Qual Nereid responde, e com quais configurações?

Mandate · mandate createbuilt #1273

A GitHub App is a Mandate of the github Nereid

Mandate · mandate createpronto #1273

Um GitHub App é um Mandate do Nereid github

~/example
# The App's identity, bound to the Reef$ nereus mandate create github \    --reef authentication \    --nereid github \    --param appId=123456 \    --param privateKey=github-app-key \    --param allow=nereus-system:*:contents=read \    --param allow=example:example/app:metadata=read \    --default✓ core/mandates/github created (reef: authentication, nereid: github, default)  clusterrole/controller-github configured (nereid github writes the status of mandate github) Next steps:   nereus mandate list
Mandate · mandate applybuilt

apply creates or changes a Mandate's params

Mandate · mandate applypronto

O apply cria ou muda os params de um Mandate

~/example

Config

Which settings does the platform keep?

Config

Quais configurações a plataforma guarda?

Config · config setbuilt

Your current owner, in the CLI's own config

Config · config setpronto

O seu owner atual, na config do próprio CLI

~/example
# The node the next commands are for$ nereus config set owner project/triton✓ config: owner = project/triton
Config · config getbuilt

Read it back, with no cluster

Config · config getpronto

Leia de volta, sem cluster

~/example
# The current owner$ nereus config get ownerproject/triton # None set: the line says how$ nereus config get owner✗ owner is not set: nereus config set owner project/<name>
Config · config slo showbuilt

The SLO of init, from the cluster or its default

Config · config slo showpronto

O SLO do init, do cluster ou o seu padrão

~/example
# Each value and where it came from$ nereus config slo showSETTING    VALUE  SOURCElocal      8m     defaultcloud      20m    defaultyellow     50%    defaultorange     75%    defaultred        100%   defaulttolerance  20%    default
Config · config slo setbuilt

Change some values; the rest keep their defaults

Config · config slo setpronto

Mude alguns valores; o resto mantém o seu padrão

~/example
# A tighter objective on k3d, and a smaller tolerance$ nereus config slo set \    --local 4m \    --tolerance 5SETTING    VALUE  SOURCElocal      4m     clustercloud      20m    defaultyellow     50%    defaultorange     75%    defaultred        100%   defaulttolerance  5%     cluster
Config · config slo resetbuilt

Back to the defaults

Config · config slo resetpronto

De volta aos padrões

~/example
# Delete the SLO from the cluster$ nereus config slo reset✓ SLO reset: every value is back to its default
Config · config installation showbuilt

Every installation has a name, an id and an alias

Config · config installation showpronto

Toda instalação tem um nome, um id e um alias

~/example
# This installation$ nereus config installation showNAME            ALIAS           IDnereus-local  nereus-local  04d6e336-7dcb-42ab-926a-2595099d5336
Config · config installation setbuilt

Change the alias or a naming override; name and id stay

Config · config installation setpronto

Mude o alias ou um naming override; nome e id ficam

~/example
# A new alias$ nereus config installation set \    --alias "Acme Prod"✓ installation nereus-local  alias = Acme Prod✓ file ~/.config/nereus/init.yaml  updated # A name instead of a generated one that is taken$ nereus config installation set \    --naming-override issuer.storage=acmeissuers01✓ installation nereus-local  naming.overrides.issuer.storage = acmeissuers01✓ file ~/.config/nereus/init.yaml  updated # The address people log in at, when it is not the ingress's$ nereus config installation set \    --public-url https://nereus.example.com✓ installation nereus-local  publicUrl = https://nereus.example.com✓ file ~/.config/nereus/init.yaml  updated
MCP

Which tools does claude.ai get?

MCP

Quais ferramentas o claude.ai recebe?

MCP · mcp tool listbuilt

The tools the Reefs offer at /mcp, each on or off

MCP · mcp tool listpronto

As ferramentas que os Reefs oferecem em /mcp, cada uma ligada ou desligada

~/example
# The tools you may call, the core's status first$ nereus mcp tool listREEF           TOOL                 STATEcore           status               onpresentations  presentations_list   onpresentations  presentations_share  off (write)
MCP · mcp tool enable | disablebuilt

An admin chooses which tools the instance offers

MCP · mcp tool enable | disablepronto

Um admin escolhe quais ferramentas a instância oferece

~/example
# Stop offering one tool$ nereus mcp tool disable presentations_list✓ tool presentations_list disabled for the instance # Offer every tool of a Reef; the name above still wins$ nereus mcp tool enable 'presentations_*'✓ tools presentations_* enabled for the instance! presentations_list stays off: disabled by its own name, which beats a pattern
MCP · mcp client add | list | removebuilt

The instance's /mcp in Claude Code, with one command

MCP · mcp client add | list | removepronto

O /mcp da instância no Claude Code, com um comando

~/example
# Add the instance's MCP server to Claude Code$ nereus mcp client add claude-code✓ claude-code: MCP server nereus added (https://nereus.example.com/mcp, scope user, OAuth client claude-code) Next steps:   claude    # then /mcp, and log in to nereus # The coding agents that have it, one row per server$ nereus mcp client listCLIENT       SERVER  REEFS  URL                             SCOPEclaude-code  nereus  all    https://nereus.example.com/mcp  user
MCP · mcp local add | list | enable | disablebuilt

The CLI as the agent's own MCP server, its tools in groups

MCP · mcp local add | list | enable | disablepronto

O CLI como o servidor MCP do próprio agente, suas ferramentas em grupos

~/example
# Register the CLI in Claude Code once, with the room's hooks$ nereus mcp local add✓ nereus-local added to claude-code (user scope): MCP server `mcp local serve`, hooks PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit Next steps:   nereus mcp local enable rooms    # inside a Claude Code session, from the agent's Bash tool # Inside a session: its groups of tools$ nereus mcp local listGROUP  STATE  TOOLSrooms  off    whoami, list_agents, post_room, read_room # Turn the room's tools on for this session$ nereus mcp local enable rooms \    --agent speo✓ rooms on: the session sees its tools now # And off$ nereus mcp local disable rooms✓ rooms off
